summary.text: Gabe Vasquez is the Democratic incumbent for New Mexico's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in November 2022 when he defeated Republican incumbent Yvette Herrell. A Las Cruces native, he worked as a journalist, chamber of commerce executive and staffer for Sen. Martin Heinrich before serving on the Las Cruces City Council. He describes his focus as lowering the cost of living, expanding health care access, protecting public lands, and immigration reform.

paragraphs.text: Born in Las Cruces, New Mexico, where he lives. His official biography describes him as a first-generation Mexican-American who grew up in the borderlands and was the first in his family born in the United States.
Earned a bachelor's degree in English and journalism from New Mexico State University in 2008.

Worked as a journalist and in public relations, and as executive director of the Las Cruces Hispano Chamber of Commerce; his official biography also cites work in public lands conservation and as a policy advocate on child welfare at the federal level.
In 2013, after helping build a Las Cruces startup company, joined Sen. Martin Heinrich's staff as a field representative working across southern New Mexico, according to his official biography.
Elected to the Las Cruces City Council in 2017, representing District 3; his official biography says he won with more than 70 percent of the vote.
Won the 2nd Congressional District seat in November 2022, defeating incumbent Yvette Herrell 50.3% to 49.6%, and took office in January 2023.
Defeated Herrell again in 2024, 52.1% to 47.9%, in a district that Donald Trump won with 49.9% of the vote.
In the 119th Congress, serves on the Committee on Agriculture (Conservation Research and Biotechnology) and the Committee on Armed Services (Readiness; Strategic Forces).
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary for the seat.
